symptom: Install job 364051 preempted twice on spot hopper-cpu (8 and 13 min in); install.sh restarted from rm -rf venv each time.
root_cause: hopper-cpu is spot; --qos=low jobs are preempted and requeued from the top of the script.
fix: install.sh made resumable (venv wiped only on the first attempt) and UV_LINK_MODE=copy dropped so uv hardlinks from the /fsx cache; fresh submit 364109 took ~2 min.

symptom: causal-conv1d 'installed' in 57 ms from a wheel in the shared uv cache that was built against another venv's torch.
root_cause: uv caches --no-build-isolation source builds keyed on the package version, not on the torch ABI they were compiled against.
fix: --no-cache --reinstall-package causal-conv1d plus an explicit import causal_conv1d_cuda in the install check.

symptom: No causal-conv1d wheel for torch 2.14 + cu130; the forced source build failed on hopper-cpu with FileNotFoundError for nvcc.
root_cause: causal-conv1d v1.7.0 ships prebuilt wheels only up to torch 2.10, and a build needs nvcc + g++ (GPU nodes only here). TRL's tree packing and transformers' Qwen3.5 fast path call causal_conv1d_fn, otherwise a slow torch conv runs.
fix: Built the wheel on hopper-dev (job 364159, ~9.5 min, sm_90 + sm_100) into stable-bench-src/wheels/torch2.14-cu130-py312; install.sh reuses it. The TRL install has to run on a GPU node.

symptom: First GPU smoke 364162 died in w1-S.py before training.
root_cause: Our kernel-binding probe assumed plain functions; transformers' hub-kernel decorator wraps causal_conv1d_fn / torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule in a kernels Func nn.Module with no __qualname__.
fix: Probe follows Func.forward's closure and is non-fatal.

symptom: vLLM 0.33 took 922 s to become healthy on a cold start; ~270 s of engine init was FlashInfer JIT ('precompiled kernels are missing ... flashinfer-cubin not installed').
root_cause: vLLM's PyPI wheel does not depend on FlashInfer's precompiled kernel packages, so every cold start JIT-compiles them. The other ~7 min are Python imports from /fsx across 8 API servers + engine cores (see all-014).
fix: install.sh installs flashinfer-jit-cache==0.7.2.post1+cu130 from flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130; warm start 357 s with engine init 36 s.

symptom: Install job 364209 failed to resolve flashinfer-cubin==0.7.2.post1; the dependent smoke went DependencyNeverSatisfied and had to be cancelled and requeued with its b200-queue waiter.
root_cause: flashinfer-cubin has no 0.7.x release on PyPI (stops at 0.6.9), while flashinfer-python is at 0.7.2.post1.
fix: Install only flashinfer-jit-cache==0.7.2.post1+cu130 from flashinfer.ai (job 364215).

symptom: 351 ServerDisconnectedError retries (rollout/vllm_retry_total) in the first rollout wave of smoke 364223; every request succeeded on retry 1 or 2 of 3, none lost.
root_cause: The AsyncGRPO rollout worker opens up to 1024 concurrent requests at once against 8 vLLM API servers at startup; the client retry budget is 3. Latent crash on a slower server.
fix: None needed for the benchmark (recovered). Release candidate fix: ramp concurrency at startup or raise/back off retries.

symptom: vLLM logs 'ParallelLMHead: Failed to load weights' (layerwise.py:266) at every weight sync.
root_cause: Qwen3.5-2B ties lm_head to embed_tokens and TRL's sync sends no lm_head tensor; vLLM warns although the tied head is updated through the embedding (IS ratio mean 1.000). Ruling out a sync bug took reading the sync path and checking IS ratios.
fix: None (cosmetic, verified). Release candidate fix: skip tied params cleanly or silence the warning.

symptom: Adaptive concurrency, zero-std group dropping and token-budget batching can't be turned off from the config, and tree attention is hard-wired; TRL can't express 'the next 32 complete groups' (step is token-sized and zero-std groups are always dropped, which amounts to refill).
root_cause: AsyncGRPO on main exposes no public switch for these behaviours; the only route is a loop_cls override.
fix: Bench code uses loop_cls overrides (group-mean advantages, spans, fixed concurrency) plus a callback; the batching gap is recorded in EQUIVALENCE.md. Leave-one-out ablations need loop_cls overrides or new config knobs.

symptom: LoRA adapter-only weight sync only works with vLLM DP=1.
root_cause: Limitation of AsyncGRPO's adapter sync path (found while mapping the ablations).
fix: None; recorded for the ablation plan.

symptom: git submodule update --init deps/prime-envs failed: .gitmodules uses git@github.com URLs (no SSH key), then 'git-lfs: not found' during checkout.
root_cause: README Manual Setup assumes an SSH GitHub key and git-lfs; only scripts/install.sh applies the HTTPS rewrite.
fix: HTTPS insteadOf rewrite and the lfs filter disabled for the checkout (lfs files are env data we don't use).

symptom: mamba-ssm (git f577286) 'built' on the CPU node with no CUDA extension (.so missing) and no error.
root_cause: mamba-ssm's build silently skips the extension when no CUDA toolkit is present. Only Nemotron-H needs it, so W1 is unaffected.
fix: None for W1; a GPU-node rebuild would be needed for Nemotron-H.

symptom: Install job 364061 preempted on spot hopper-cpu during the import check, after the cold import of torch/vllm/fla from /fsx had already run 11+ min without finishing.
root_cause: Spot preemption plus slow cold imports from /fsx on CPU nodes.
fix: Cancelled the requeued copy; import check moved into the first GPU job (378 s cold, 111 s warm).

symptom: Our Qwen3.5 check failed or gave meaningless results three times: from_pretrained raised 'no attribute all_tied_weights_keys', then to_empty() untied lm_head so all logits were zero and the packing comparison read 0.0000 everywhere.
root_cause: The check did not mirror the trainer's path (meta build, FSDP shard, DCP load from HF, tie asserted before load).
fix: Check rewritten to follow the trainer sequence, re-tie and assert, with a negative control.

symptom: After import prime_rl, transformers' Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration fails in the same process: 'Qwen3_5VisionConfig' object has no attribute 'rope_parameters'.
root_cause: Importing prime_rl registers its own Qwen3.5 config classes with AutoConfig, a global side effect at import time.
fix: HF reference run moved to a subprocess. Trainer unaffected.

root_cause: logger.info(..., flush=True) on the hybrid_engine=False path of V1 separate_async; in v0.9.1 that documented setting can't run at all. Fixed upstream in ace775e8 (#7926), not in any tag.

root_cause: Our eval-mode forward defaulted to use_cache=True, which verl's packed GDN patch rejects by design (training runs use_cache=False).

symptom: Recipe job 364206 hung after ray.init with nothing in the job log.
root_cause: Our common.sh gave Ray a 90-port worker range; on an exclusive 92-CPU node Ray prestarts 92 workers, the extra ones fail with 'No available ports' and the TaskRunner never gets a worker (found only in /tmp/ray session logs).

symptom: Recipe jobs 364231 (step 1) and 364302 (step 6) crashed with KeyError: 'loss_mask' not found in TensorDict in compute_log_prob, each right after a validation pass.
root_cause: TransferQueue (verl's always-on data plane in v0.9.1) logs 'Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s' (38 and 304 times) and carries on, so data is silently never marked ready and a later shard comes back empty. A 1,319-prompt validation on top of a 5,120-rollout batch floods the controller.
fix: TQ_DATA_UPDATE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT=600 exported for every verl job (env knob, no code patch).

symptom: The recommended-arm config couldn't inherit from w1-S.yaml: 'Overriding hydra.searchpath is only supported from the primary config'.

symptom: Rollout config carries fixed ports localhost:50123/50124 (TransferQueue/Mooncake metadata and master server).

symptom: verl's W1 chain waiters 364379 (19:29) and 364422 (19:47) died to hopper-cpu NODE_FAIL.
root_cause: Spot CPU node failures.

root_cause: Our chain design: afterany advances on a dead waiter; --no-requeue on spot nodes stops the chain for good.
fix: afterok for the recipe step, then b200-queue AFTER_RUNNING gates with requeue-safe waiters.

symptom: Install job 364058 preempted on spot hopper-cpu after 6 min of downloads and requeued.

root_cause: Installing math-verify[antlr4_13_2] for the shared reward replaced antlr4 4.9.3, which omegaconf (imported everywhere in SkyRL) needs. Even with the antlr4_9_3 extra, uv kept 4.13.2 until an explicit pin.

symptom: GSM8K smoke 364285 died in ray start: 'The current node timed out during startup ... GCS cannot find the node'.
root_cause: Our launcher: 90 worker ports, no --num-gpus or --object-store-memory (Ray sizes the object store from the 2 TB host RAM), dashboard on, on a shared node. Raylet logs were in node-local /tmp and lost.
fix: 1000-port blocks, explicit --num-gpus, --object-store-memory=40GiB, --include-dashboard=false, Ray logs copied to <run>/ray_logs on failure.

symptom: Second smoke 364292: driver ray.init could not reach GCS ('Failed to connect to GCS ... within 5 seconds').
root_cause: Our head bound to 127.0.0.1 while RAY_ADDRESS resolved to the node IP.
fix: Head started with --node-ip-address=$(hostname -I | first) and RAY_ADDRESS exported with that IP, as OpenRLHF's launcher does.

symptom: With SkyRL's default remove_microbatch_padding=true on FSDP, the second sample of a packed micro-batch is off by up to 2.38 nats vs the sample alone (0.20-0.25 unpacked). No error or warning.
root_cause: SkyRL's FSDP packing passes only position_ids; transformers' Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet honours boundaries only with cu_seq_lens_q, so GDN state leaks across samples. Nothing guards against it; only the Qwen3.5 example script turns packing off.
fix: remove_microbatch_padding=false and micro-batch 1 in both W1 arms (correct, slower). Megatron's THD path is SkyRL's packed route for Qwen3.5, unused here.

symptom: Pre-train eval sat at 0% GPU for 7+ min; total eval 8.3 min in smoke 364362.
root_cause: data.dataloader.num_workers defaults to 8 with multiprocessing_context='spawn', re-created per dataloader iteration; each worker re-imports the 20 GB venv from /fsx. The docstring itself recommends 0.
fix: data.dataloader.num_workers=0 in the W1 configs and smoke script.

symptom: A warning every 5 s from trainer.enable_ray_gpu_monitor.
root_cause: The monitor scrapes the Ray dashboard metrics endpoint, which a dashboard-less head (needed on shared nodes) doesn't serve; it only feeds wandb.
fix: trainer.enable_ray_gpu_monitor=false.

symptom: W1 smoke 364341 (8 GPUs) failed at trainer init 17 min after job start: FullyAsyncRayPPOTrainer rejects policy_loss_type=regular.
root_cause: Fully async requires a loss on rollout logprobs (rollout_is, dppo, reinforce, cispo). The constraint is sound, but it is checked only after Ray, vLLM engines and the FSDP load are up, not at config validation.
fix: Shared arm uses policy_loss_type=rollout_is with eps 0.2/0.28 against the sampler logprobs (recorded in EQUIVALENCE.md).

symptom: run_gsm8k.sh as shipped on main no longer runs the objective behind the published 0.796 GSM8K result (inferred from the default changes; the repro was not run).
root_cause: Main changed defaults in #2635 (policy_loss_type regular->dppo, loss_reduction token_mean->prompt_mean, grpo_norm_by_std True->False); the recipe script and docs predate it.
fix: Repro must pass policy_loss_type=regular loss_reduction=token_mean grpo_norm_by_std=true (planned, not run yet).

symptom: With --ds.packing_samples, a 500-token sample packed after a 3000-token one differs from the sample alone by max |dlogp| 7.94 (mean 2.24); at RL level vllm_kl was 0.18-0.25 packed vs 0.0003-0.0006 unpacked. No error or warning.

symptom: hopper-cpu install jobs pended on Resources/Priority (TRL 16 CPU / 64 GB, SkyRL 28 CPU / 100 GB, verl 64 GB).
root_cause: We asked for more than spot nodes advertise (~55 GB free on most).
fix: Shrunk in place (scontrol update NumCPUs=8 MinMemoryNode=24000 or 32000); rule: <= 8 CPUs / 24-32 GB on hopper-cpu.

symptom: srun steps in b200-queue GPU jobs were capped at 2 GiB / 1 CPU; miles' checkpoint conversion thrashed at ~2,000 major page faults/s for 15+ min (job 364201).
root_cause: b200-queue's 1-CPU / 2 GB waiter called sbatch with --export=ALL, leaking SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE=2048, SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK=1, SLURM_TRES_PER_TASK into every GPU job.
fix: b200-queue-inner unsets SLURM_*/SBATCH_*/SRUN_* before submitting; verified by envcheck job. Earlier jobs use srun --mem=0 --cpus-per-task=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE.

symptom: A preempted spot waiter (364219) was requeued and submitted TRL's smoke a second time (364273).

symptom: prime-rl's recommended arm (364392) started before its shared arm (364425), so prime-rl held two nodes and a third duplicate waiter (364428) was armed; OpenRLHF waiters were named 'q-' with a basename error.

fix: Waiters named q-<lib dir>-<script>-<args>; read job ids from squeue or the queue log, never from the name.

root_cause: b200-queue names its job q-<last argument>, so my shared-arm queue job was q-shared (364371). I chained the recommended arm on q-w1 364369, which was another library's queue job; it failed at 19:16 and released the chain.

symptom: W1-S shared run 364684 FAILED at step 9/200, ~30 min after start: rank 0 raised 'RuntimeError: Rollout worker heartbeat stale: 300s > 300s; child is hung.' (async_rollout_worker.py:1627) while waiting on the sample queue; the other ranks died on a gloo 'Connection closed by peer'. Last logged step had rollout_queue_size 90 (22.8 one step earlier).
root_cause: Our shared reward (workloads/math/reward.py:37) disables math_verify's SIGALRM timeouts off the main thread; AsyncGRPO runs a sync reward via asyncio.to_thread (async_rollout_worker.py:1339), so a completion like \boxed{10^{10^{10}}} made sympy hold the GIL computing a huge integer, freezing the rollout child's event loop and heartbeat. Reproduced 5/6 on CPU with the real AsyncRolloutWorker and a fake server, with and without our span logger (envs/trl/HANG_364684.md).
fix: Harness: math_reward made async def so it runs on the event loop's main thread with timeouts on (patches/harness/w1-S-async-reward.patch; repro 364860 healthy for 120 s / 35.6k requests).

symptom: W1-S shared 364425 finished training (COMPLETED), but the post-run tools/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py crashed on every rank: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable at 'for key in getattr(model, "_tied_weights_keys", [])' (line 170); the log shows 'convert_dcp_to_bf16.py FAILED'.
root_cause: The converter assumes _tied_weights_keys is a list; on this model/transformers 5.19 the attribute exists and is None, so the getattr default never applies. Our invocation (DCP step dir + output dir) matches the tool's documented usage.
fix: Bench copy envs/prime-rl/convert_dcp_to_bf16.py falls back to dropping lm_head.weight; complete_hf.py fills any tensor missing vs the base checkpoint (rev. 6); launch/prime-rl/export.sbatch re-exports, and w1.sbatch now uses the patched copy.

symptom: W1 run 364409 logged 22 CUDACachingAllocator warnings 'memory allocation failed with OOM ... trying to allocate ~16.5 GB' on the policy actors between 19:48 and 20:45; training continued until the hang (openrlhf-008).
root_cause: Probably full-vocab logits for a 16k-token micro-batch (248k vocab, ~16 GB) near the 180 GB capacity, so the allocator frees cache and retries. Not verified whether it relates to the hang.
fix: None yet; check alloc retries and step time on the rerun (364704).

symptom: vLLM logs 'Attempted to load weight <name> with dtype torch.float32 into parameter with dtype torch.bfloat16' (utils.py) for every synced tensor on every weight sync: ~1.7k lines per tensor type across the smoke and W1 logs, the top TRL warnings by count.
root_cause: AsyncGRPO's weight sync sends the fp32 master weights and vLLM casts them to bf16 on load, so each sync moves 2x the bytes and floods the log. Measured sync time is still ~0.2 s on the 2B model, so the cost is small at this size.
fix: None for the benchmark. Release candidate: cast to the engine dtype before sending.

symptom: W1 rerun 364704 hung like 364409 (openrlhf-008): step 8 generation stopped at 31/32 groups after the trainer finished step 8 (rank 0 at 64/64 micro-steps); all GPUs idle, no error or traceback, cancelled after 29 min.
root_cause: Not the trainer OOM: the trainer finished its step and waited on the VLLMLock held by the stuck generator. OpenRLHF runs a custom reward_func via asyncio.to_thread inside each vLLM rollout actor, so the shared reward's math_verify has no timeout there; answers like 9^{9^{9}} make sympy compute a huge int in C with the GIL held, freezing that actor's event loop (measured: 0 loop ticks in 60-120 s). 24/32 and 31/32 match one engine's 8 groups / one group. The exact completion wasn't captured.
fix: configs/openrlhf/w1_reward.py runs compute_score in a spawn process pool (math_verify's 5 s timeouts active on the worker main thread, 30 s hard kill, slow calls logged); w1.sbatch watchdog kills the run after 20 min of log silence. No OpenRLHF source change.

symptom: Trainer ranks hit the caching allocator's OOM-and-retry path on ~16.5 GB allocations (22 times in 364409, 3 in 364704) with 3-9 GB free of 191 GB on a 2B model.
root_cause: Actor.forward casts the full logits of a micro-batch to fp32 (16.6k x 248320 x 4 B = 16.5 GB) and has no chunked-logprob or fused linear-CE path; --ds.use_liger_kernel is refused for VLM checkpoints like Qwen3.5. Varying micro-batch lengths fragment the cache. Not the cause of the hangs (openrlhf-013).
fix: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True exported in launch/openrlhf/common.sh before ray start.

symptom: Latent, not hit in our runs: trl/rewards/accuracy_rewards.py:74-78 and 296-300 disable math_verify's timeouts off the main thread, and AsyncGRPOTrainer runs sync rewards via asyncio.to_thread in the rollout child, so accuracy_reward with a pathological answer would freeze the rollout worker exactly like trl-011.
root_cause: SIGALRM-based timeouts only work on the main thread; the reward is called from a worker thread. Making the reward async is not a general fix, because GRPOTrainer runs async rewards on a daemon thread (grpo_trainer.py:799).
fix: Not fixed. Options in envs/trl/HANG_364684.md; diagnostics patch patches/trl/rollout-worker-dump-stacks-on-stale-heartbeat.patch.

symptom: With TRL's default score centering, every request asks /v1/completions for top-8 logprobs; vLLM's API servers back up (~440 requests queued inside them), so the weight-sync /pause waits 18 s on average (max 71 s) and generated tok/s drops ~12%; trained tok/s 35.8k vs 54.1k for the shared arm (logprobs=0, pause 0.1 s).
root_cause: Per-token top-8 logprob dicts on /v1/completions (~10M live Python objects per API server at ~85 x 16k-token requests) make GC passes and response building stall each server's event loop; /pause and finished replies queue behind it. prime-rl sends the same /pause on the same topology in 0.048 s because it uses /inference/v1/generate with flat logprobs and no detokenization. The slow path is in vLLM's /v1/completions top-k logprob handling, which TRL's default selects.
fix: Not fixed. num_sampler_logprobs=2 removed the stall (50.3 s/step, 0.67 s pause vs 65.6 s / 19.4 s at k=8, run 365383) but the user rejected it: too few logprobs for score centering. Remaining options: vLLM serving config (--api-server-count 16 measured 0.06 s mean pause at k=8 in the repro), or a vLLM/TRL-side change to how top-k logprobs are produced and returned.

root_cause: remote_inference_client._post (remote_inference_client.py:325-355) parses every response body with orjson; after its retries it re-raised the decode error of a non-JSON body (3 server 5xx lines in the log around 06:30), and the fully async trainer treats any generator worker exception as fatal.

symptom: Every HF export of W1-S shared run 364970 has lm_head.weight != embed_tokens.weight (relative difference 2.4e-4 at step 50, 5.5e-4 at step 200) although Qwen3.5-2B has tie_word_embeddings=true; the trainer trains two matrices while vLLM keeps one shared matrix and skips lm_head.weight on load and sync.
root_cause: FSDPStrategy._fsdp_init_model moves the module to meta before apply_fsdp2 and never re-ties; module.to('meta') gives lm_head and embed_tokens separate parameters (reproduced on CPU with torch 2.13: tied after from_pretrained, untied after .to('meta'), tied again after tie_weights()). Affects every tied-embedding model on SkyRL's FSDP backend.
fix: Not applied. One line upstream: module.tie_weights() right after module.to(torch.device('meta')). Measured effect on run 364970: sampler vs trainer mean |dlogp| 0.004-0.014 nats, no token outside (0.8, 1.28); not the cause of that run's collapse.

symptom: W1-S shared run 364970 collapsed twice: train reward 0.6 -> 0.01-0.05 by steps 88-95 and again by step 200; eval AIME24/AIME25/MATH-500 0.027/0.021/0.120 at step 100 and 0.006/0.023/0.248 at step 200 (base 0.212/0.171/0.776). Answers degrade into near-empty outputs and a re-opened '<think></think>:' prefix. The rollout_is out-of-band share compounds from 0.2% (step 30) to 60% (step 93), and the trainer-vs-sampler gap goes from 0.013 to 2.9 nats at constant staleness 4.
root_cause: Probable: our shared-arm mapping used PPO's 0.2/0.28 clip epsilons as rollout_is's two-sided mask band, which also zeroes the restoring gradient on tokens that drift against their advantage. SkyRL's own fully async recipe uses a (0.5, 5.0) band plus a 0.99-1.01 geometric sequence mask. Ruled out: exports, staleness, step-1 numerics, and untied embeddings (0.004-0.014 nats). Not yet proven: the DPPO control (365013) crashed at step 36, and an A/B from the step-50 export is queued.
fix: Rerun the shared arm with a one-sided PPO-clip loss against the sampler logprobs (custom 'ppo_rollout' registered through SkyRL's public PolicyLossRegistry, no source patch; code in stable-bench-runs/skyrl/collapse-364970/collapse_main.py). Move this row to lib if the queued A/B shows the one-sided loss drifting too.

symptom: SkyRL's Harbor entrypoint always deep-merges CLI overrides into its default.yaml (Daytona, override_cpus=1, 1 GB memory/storage, a Daytona-only kwarg), so those keys can't be removed for another sandbox backend.
root_cause: main_harbor.py loads default.yaml and merges overrides on top; no way to replace it.

symptom: Stock HarborGenerator would zero the loss of almost every W2 group: an agent timeout masks its whole group of 8, and ~40-50% of 9B episodes hit the 600 s budget.
root_cause: _harbor_agent_loop treats AgentTimeoutError as a failure (no retry, loss mask 0) although Harbor still verifies the episode and terminus-2 keeps its rollout details; build_step_wise_generator_output then masks the group.
fix: skyrl_w2_main.py overrides _harbor_agent_loop: a timed-out episode with a verifier result is trained with its score (SHARED_W2). Failed episodes still zero their group (SkyRL behaviour, recorded).

symptom: With remove_microbatch_padding=false and one sequence per micro-batch, every sample is still forwarded at the step's global padded width (max prompt + max response over the batch).
root_cause: SampleBasedBatchIterator uses TensorBatch.chunk, which slices rows but never trims padding columns; only remove_microbatch_padding=true unpads.
fix: W2 uses remove_microbatch_padding=true with micro-batch 1 (unpadded, no cross-sample packing, so no GDN leak). W1 configs still pad: their throughput and EQUIVALENCE 'nothing is padded' are off.

symptom: A custom policy loss registered through PolicyLossRegistry that only reads rollout logprobs (ppo_rollout) still gets a full no-grad policy forward over every sample.
root_cause: _skip_policy_forward checks a fixed set LOSSES_WITHOUT_OLD_LOGPROBS keyed on built-in loss types; registered losses can't declare they don't need old logprobs.
fix: W2Trainer._skip_policy_forward returns True for ppo_rollout under SkyRL's own conditions.

symptom: workloads/agentic/sweep.sh only spared trl-w2*/w2-validate* jobs, so TRL's end-of-job sweep would have cancelled a running SkyRL W2 job's sandboxes.
root_cause: The sweep pattern was written before a second library ran W2; sandboxes carry no per-job tag.
fix: Pattern now also matches skyrl-w2*.

symptom: verifiers' docker runtime fails every Harbor task at test staging on a rootless engine: 'tar: test.sh: Cannot change ownership to uid 150231 ... Invalid argument' (vf-validate, job 365382).
root_cause: HarborTask.stage_tests packs tests/ with tarfile (host uid in the headers) and unpacks with 'tar -xzf' as root, which restores ownership; a uid outside the container's user namespace can't be restored. setup() in the same file passes --no-same-owner, stage_tests doesn't.

symptom: verifiers' terminus_2 harness builds Harbor's Terminus2 with fixed arguments: summarisation stays on (enable_summarize=True, proactive threshold 8000 free tokens) and there is no max_turns / max_output_tokens / temperature kwarg.
root_cause: harnesses/terminus_2/program.py passes only model, api_base, api_key, record_terminal_session=False, interleaved_thinking=True; the harness config has only dialect and version.
fix: Budgets go through verifiers' own AgentConfig (max_turns=30, max_turn_tokens=8192, timeout.rollout=600), which worked (stop=max_turns at 30 turns, job 365405). Summarisation can't be turned off: recorded as a W2 gap.

symptom: HarborTaskset can't take a local directory of Harbor tasks: it always runs 'harbor download <dataset> --export' from a registry and caches the export under ~/.cache/harbor/<name>.
root_cause: dataset_dir() only knows registry selectors (dataset, repo, registry_path, registry_url).
fix: Pre-fill the cache: ~/.cache/harbor/termgrade-local -> the local task dir, then --env.taskset.dataset termgrade-local (dataset_dir returns an existing cache dir as is).

symptom: miles' in-process Harbor path has no local backend it supports: HARBOR_ENV_TYPE=docker is rejected by launch_common.py ('docker needs a Docker daemon next to Trial.run()'), its credential wiring and verified providers are cloud only (Daytona, E2B, Modal, Novita, AgentENV), and its OpenEnv tbench2 connectors are cloud or a Docker-SDK shared server.

symptom: W2 can't run on verl as shipped on any sandbox backend: verl has no Harbor, terminal-task or OpenEnv integration and no container sandbox for agent episodes.
root_cause: verl ships a generic AgentLoop API, SandboxFusion (code-execution reward only) and verl-recipe swe_agent (SWE-agent via SWE-ReX docker, SWE-bench style); none runs Harbor tasks or terminus-2.
fix: None under the benchmark rule (it would need our own AgentLoop or model-proxy recipe code). verl W2 is reported as not runnable as shipped.

symptom: Container pulls from Docker Hub fail with 'toomanyrequests: You have reached your unauthenticated pull rate limit' (job 365369).
root_cause: All anonymous pulls leave through the cluster NAT and share one Docker Hub quota.

symptom: On the Ubuntu 22.04 GPU nodes (podman 3.4.4) an attached 'docker run --rm' through podman's Docker-compat socket never returns after the container exits, and Harbor's docker env fails with 'CNI network ... not found' on the compose-created network (jobs 365394, 365405). The CPU nodes' podman 4.9.3 has neither problem.

fix: A docker CLI shim (container-tools/shim/docker) runs '--rm' containers without --rm and removes them after; verifiers' docker runtime then works. Harbor's docker env stays unusable on these nodes; use Harbor's singularity env there. A newer podman would fix both but needs a third-party binary (not installed).

symptom: Harbor's singularity environment fails every trial with 'Server process died' / '[runtime] FATAL: cannot bootstrap pip' (job 365389).
root_cause: Its default singularity_no_mount='home,tmp,bind-paths' also drops Apptainer's /etc/resolv.conf bind here, so the in-box bootstrap can't resolve bootstrap.pypa.io (job 365392 compares the variants).
fix: singularity_no_mount=home,tmp (a shipped env kwarg: Harbor --ek, miles HARBOR_ENV_KWARGS, SkyRL environment.kwargs). Oracle reward 1.0 after (365393).

symptom: The obvious per-call output cap for an agent, env.agent.max_turn_tokens, also ends the episode at the first length-capped reply; SHARED_W2 (and Harbor's terminus-2) cap the call and continue.
root_cause: verifiers' AgentConfig.max_turn_tokens both caps max_tokens and adds a max_turn_tokens stop condition (configs/agent.py docstring).
fix: Use [orchestrator.train.sampling] max_completion_tokens = 8192, which caps each call without a stop condition (configs/prime-rl/w2-M.toml).
